h: "Make Me a Small Meal": The Trunk of the Tree

p: It is brought in the Midrash
A parable of a king who made a feast
for his servants for seven days,
and afterwards said to his son,
so that I may have enjoyment from you."
So too, on the seven days of the festival
corresponding to the nations of the world,
and on Shemini Atzeres one bull,
even the aspect of a servant's service
to His service, may He be blessed.
that all the seven days of the festival,
through the action of performing mitzvos,
with the sukkah and the four species,
to draw down the inner light and the surrounding light
which is the aspect of a servant's service:
and in the service of the heart,
the meal of the branches of the Tree,
for the performance of the mitzvos
are called by the name of branches,
which branch out and surround the root.
it is the meal of the Trunk of the Tree,
of the tree of the Tree of Life,
which is called the aspect of a son.
And therefore there is no need
for any action of performing a mitzvah
to hint that the surrounding lights enter within
which becomes fixed in the innermost
And this is also hinted in
what is said in the name of
זֵכֶר צַדִּיק וְקָדוֹשׁ לִבְרָכָה לְחַיֵּי הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא,
may the memory of the righteous and holy be a blessing for the life of the World to Come,
that the day of Shemini Atzeres
וְהַיְינוּ כִּי כָּל שִׁבְעַת יְמֵי הֶחָג
That is because all seven days of the festival
were through the performance of mitzvos
and especially on the seventh day of the festival,
which is the Ushpiza of David,
who is the very essence of the aspect of prayer,
But on the day of Shemini Atzeres
we come to the completion of the purpose,
that the words of Torah enter the heart,
as is brought in the Tikkunim
that on this day is the wellspring of the Torah,
and then we do not need
in "A Song of Ascents, of Shlomo"
"If Hashem does not build the house,
its builders have toiled on it in vain,"
because this is the very essence
of the aspect of Shlomo HaMelech, peace be upon him:
that all the actions and all the service
except when Hashem, may He be blessed,
makes the words of Torah shine
and then there is no need
so He gives to His beloved in sleep"
That is, one who is bound
to Hashem, may He be blessed,
he is bound to Him, may He be blessed,
in a dream of the night,
and said, 'Ask what I shall give you'"
the aspect of calling out and prayer,
only that one is answered immediately,
"Hashem is near to all who call upon Him,
to all who call upon Him in truth"
And for this reason we begin the hakafos with
for Hashem, may He be blessed,
that is bound to Him, may He be blessed,

paragraphs.text: Parallel: R. Yosef Chaim of Baghdad, Ben Yehoyada, Sukkah 55b — “‘Make me a small meal, so that I may have enjoyment from you’: if the meal is large, people will say he came because of the enjoyment of the meal, since it is great; but if the meal is small, with no real measure of enjoyment, they will not say he came for it, but ‘I came for your sake.’ And so it is in what the parable represents.” Connection: Ben Yehoyada explains why the meal of the eighth day is small: its smallness shows that the bond itself is the point, as Rav Tzadok explains the day that belongs to Israel alone.

paragraphs.text: Taanis 2a — "From where do we know it is with prayer? As it was taught: 'To love Hashem your God and to serve Him with all your heart' (Devarim 11:13) — what is the service that is in the heart? You must say: this is prayer."

paragraphs.text: Zohar III 96a (Emor) — "'On the eighth day an Atzeres' — what is Atzeres? The place where all are bound as one is called Atzeres, a gathering… All those days were the days of the meals of the branches of the Tree, and therefore seventy bulls; afterward is the joy of the body of the Tree itself and the joy of the Torah, and for its sake it is one day, Atzeres — the joy of the Torah."

paragraphs.text: Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 13, 29b — "Shemini Atzeres is a festival in its own right; on it is the welling forth of the Torah, to water the tree that is planted in the garden, and its roots and branches are like the circle (chug) of the earth, for all the festivals are celebrated in it."

paragraphs.text: Berachos 5b — "Rabbi Yochanan said: Granted Torah and kindness, as it is written, 'Through kindness and truth iniquity is atoned' (Mishlei 16:6): 'kindness' is acts of kindness… and 'truth' is Torah, as it is said, 'Buy truth and do not sell it' (Mishlei 23:23)."
